pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: A pelvic ultrasound revealing a 4 cm mature ovarian cystic teratoma containing neural tissue, in combination with the pathognomonic EEG 'Extreme Delta Brush' pattern. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The ectopic neural elements within the ovarian teratoma express N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, which trigger a systemic autoimmune response. The patient produces IgG autoantibodies specifically directed against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. These antibodies bind, cross-link, and cause the reversible internalization of cell-surface NMDA receptors in the brain. The resulting loss of NMDA receptor function leads to a breakdown of GABAergic inhibitory pathways, causing the characteristic sequence of psychosis, dyskinesias, autonomic breakdown, and hypoventilation. Surgical excision of the teratoma alongside immunotherapy (plasmapheresis, IVIG, or rituximab) offers a high rate of recovery.
